title: Resolve Merge Conflicts in Design Document
description:
You are resolving merge conflicts in a technical design document. Two developers (A and B) independently edited design_v1.md, creating conflicting changes. The file design_conflicted.md contains the base document with 12 merge conflict markers.

Each conflict is marked with:
```
<<<<<<< LOCAL (Developer A)
[Developer A's version]
=======
[Developer B's version]
>>>>>>> REMOTE (Developer B)
```

Resolve ALL 12 conflicts using these rules:

1. When both sides are identical: take either version (they agree)
2. When one side only fixes a typo/spelling while the other ALSO adds substantive improvements (extra detail, better wording, or updated values): take the more comprehensive version
3. When both sides make different substantive changes (different numbers, different approaches): prefer the REMOTE (Developer B) version

After resolving:
- There should be NO conflict markers remaining in the output
- All 12 conflicts should be resolved
- The rest of the document (non-conflicted parts) must remain exactly as-is
- Do not add any new content or make any changes outside the conflict regions

You have access to a document comparison tool at: TOOL_PATH/doccompare.py
The conflicted file is at: WORK_DIR/design_conflicted.md
The original (pre-conflict) file is at: WORK_DIR/design_v1.md (for reference)

Write the resolved result to: WORK_DIR/output.md
notes: This task tests the agent's ability to find and resolve merge conflicts scattered through a ~500-line document. The CLI agent can search for conflict markers (grep for '<<<<<<<'), process them one at a time, and verify all markers are removed. The diff-only agent must find all 12 conflicts in a large inline document and resolve them correctly in one pass. Some conflicts are trivial (both agree), some require judgment (one-sided improvement), and some require applying the REMOTE preference rule.
